hypothesis: The remaining COLD roster scan cost (post-#2856 warm recency fix: ~70ms/1000, ~283ms/4096 sessions) is dominated NOT by syscall I/O time but by the fold's per-message userspace work: the search-text cap guard re-counted the capped corpus (chars().count()) for every user/assistant message plus two more counts per append (O(messages x 64KiB) per session), with the 8KiB-default BufReader chunking grown files into one read syscall per 8KiB as the second cost (strace census: 6.6k reads / 1k-session cold pass, 27.2k at 4,096).
approach: Two surgical commits on pa-daemon session_store.rs, neither changing a row byte: (1) SessionScanAccumulator carries search_text_chars in lockstep with the one writer; append_capped_search_text takes and returns the running count (guard + append read the O(1) counter, fold stays O(messages)); lockstep + legacy-mirror unit tests added; the info_tests legacy reference fold now inlines the TS append (independent of the product helper). (2) The fold's BufReader capacity raised to SESSION_SCAN_READ_BUF_BYTES = 64KiB (line semantics, folded bytes, and resume cursor unchanged - only syscall chunking). Baseline-first evidence: per-stage replica probe split the cold fold at each tier; strace -cf census counted cold-pass syscalls at base and candidate.
parity_notes: Row/wire parity: the char counter equals chars().count() by construction (single writer updates it from exactly the chars it appends: space + taken chars; multibyte chars counted via the char iterator), proven by the lockstep test across multibyte/cap-cut/post-cap sequences and by identical probe checksums across ALL tiers and arms (100=762089, 1000=893085, 4096=3680629 on every slot both before and after). SessionInfo rows, JSONL bytes, wire/API, replay, streaming catalog, resume/torn-tail semantics untouched; the counter rides SessionScanState clones (clone_for_resume) like the corpus string. 64KiB buffer only changes read() chunking; read_line consumes identical lines. No TS semantic is reinterpreted: TS caps the same way; this only stops re-counting. Fixture audit on both VMs: shipped many-sessions tar verified (manifest sha fcc8f70a; 1099/1100 clean + the known stale-manifest row 100/01a0dad3 whose VM bytes equal the tarball sha 39fca708); 4096 tier is byte-exact 4x+96 copies of the 1000 tier (4096/4096 sha-verified).
